zh-CN.title: 如何使用 · 等高线地形与五大典型地貌

lines: 第 1 步：点右下角「开始实验」，在立体地形里观察水平切面下降、交线形成、垂直投影与疏密判坡四步动画。
第 2 步：在立体地形上按住鼠标拖动可旋转视角，滚轮缩放；这是可交互的 3D 地形。
第 3 步：点画布上方「五大典型地貌」标签（山峰/山脊/山谷/鞍部/陡崖），画面换成对应的专门地形并叠加完整等高线，观察各自的等高线特征。
第 4 步：点底部「俯视图 / 立体图」在等高线地图与 3D 地形间切换；鼠标悬停任意位置，底部显示该点海拔与地形部位。
第 5 步：点「上色 / 取消上色」对比分层设色与纯等高线；点「全屏」进入全屏演示。
空格：播放 / 暂停实验。
数字 1 – 5：依次切换到山峰、山脊、山谷、鞍部、陡崖。
等高切割：一个水平面从山顶向下移动，与山体在同一海拔相交。
形成交线：每个水平切面留下一条闭合交线，多层交线共同描述山体起伏。
投影成图：各高度的交线沿垂线投影到同一平面，累积成完整等高线图。
疏密判坡：坡度着色叠加等高线，陡处线密、缓处线疏。
山峰：等高线闭合，数值由中心向四周递减（若向内降低则为洼地）。
山脊：等高线向海拔低处凸出（凸低为脊），脊线是分水线。
山谷：等高线向海拔高处凸出（凸高为谷），谷线是集水线，常发育河流。
鞍部：两座山峰之间相对低洼，俯视轮廓呈马鞍状收腰。
陡崖：等高线密集甚至重合，近乎垂直；n 条线重合时 (n−1)d ≤ ΔH < (n+1)d。
同一条等高线上各点海拔相等；相邻等高线之间的高差叫等高距（本图 100 米）。
等高线越密坡越陡，越疏坡越缓。
每 5 条加粗一条叫计曲线，标注海拔便于读数。
海拔：某地高出海平面的垂直距离；相对高度：两点海拔之差。
分层设色按固定高程档位套固定色阶（深绿→浅绿→绿→浅黄→黄→浅褐→褐→白）。
山峰用 ▲ 加高程数字标注；河流用蓝色线沿谷底绘制；陡崖用红色锯齿线表示。
指北针在图幅右上，比例尺在左下，分层设色图例在右下，地形剖面图在底部。

en.title: How to use · Contour Lines & Five Landforms

lines: Step 1: press Start to watch the four-step animation — contour cutting, line formation, vertical projection and slope reading.
Step 2: drag with the mouse to rotate the 3D terrain, scroll to zoom; it is fully interactive.
Step 3: click a landform tab above the canvas (peak / ridge / valley / saddle / cliff) to load its dedicated terrain with its full contour pattern.
Step 4: toggle Top view / 3D view at the bottom; hover anywhere to read elevation and terrain feature.
Step 5: use Colour / No colour to compare hypsometric tint with pure contour lines; use Fullscreen for presentation.
Space: play / pause the experiment.
Numbers 1 – 5: switch to peak, ridge, valley, saddle, cliff.
Contour cutting: a horizontal plane descends from the summit and intersects the mountain at one elevation.
Forming lines: each slice leaves a closed intersection line; stacked lines describe the relief.
Projection: intersection lines are projected vertically onto one plane, building the contour map.
Slope density: slope shading over contours — dense lines mean steep, sparse lines mean gentle.
Peak: closed contours, values decrease outward (if they decrease inward it is a depression).
Ridge: contours bulge toward lower ground; a watershed line.
Valley: contours bulge toward higher ground; a drainage line, often a stream.
Saddle: low ground between two peaks, pinched like a saddle in plan view.
Cliff: contours crowd or overlap, nearly vertical; n overlapping lines: (n−1)d ≤ ΔH < (n+1)d.
All points on one contour share the same elevation; the gap between neighbours is the contour interval (100 m here).
Closer contours mean steeper slopes; wider spacing means gentler slopes.
Every 5th contour is bolded as an index contour and labelled with elevation.
Elevation is height above sea level; relative height is the difference between two elevations.
Hypsometric tint uses fixed colour bands (dark green → light green → green → pale yellow → yellow → light brown → brown → white).
Peaks are marked with ▲ plus elevation; rivers are blue lines along valleys; cliffs use a red saw-tooth line.
North arrow top-right, scale bar bottom-left, tint legend bottom-right, terrain profile along the bottom.
